newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Upstream pushes oil earnings.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Upstream pushes oil earnings.

text.p: Strong oil and gas prices powered energy company first quarter earnings to new highs, and although refining and marketing remained weak it was that sector which generated positive earnings surprises.

Anyone with upstream exposure benefitted, from majors like Mobil Corp, DuPont Co's Conoco, Chevron Corp and Phillips Petroleum Co to service companies like Cliffs Drilling and Baker Hughes Inc, where activity roared ahead.

Mobil operating earnings rose 15 percent to $844 million and earnings per share rose to $2.11 from $1.83, with almost all of the gain coming from a $2.70 rise in U.S. crude oil prices to $18.54 and a 59 cent rise in natural gas prices to $2.75 per thousand cubic feet.
Earnings were some 15 cents above expectations although the shares were little moved, off $0.125 at $125.75 in a weaker wider market.

"The variance versus our estimate was primarily in the foreign downstream, and is consistent with the results reported by other international oil companies," said Schroder Wertheim analyst Michael Mayer.

Mobil's refining and marketing division stumbled due to domestic refinery maintenance, which cut $90 million off the division's earnings to $150 million, although the international division earnings rose $11 million to $192 million, with a strong showing in Britain.

Conoco, whose chief executive Archie Dunham described the quarter as "a fantastic start to 1997", saw upstream earnings rise 41 percent to a record $269 million as crude oil prices rose 15 percent and natural gas rose 42 percent worldwide.
Some of the price rises were offset by lower production.

Conoco had a significantly stronger quarter in the downstream sector where earnings rose 170 percent to $62 million from $23 million, although it is still not achieving the cost of capital plus 12 percent target for DuPont units.
It achieved this largely due to the favourable price differential for heavy crudes compared with sweet crudes.
At Chevron, earnings came in above expectations at $831 million versus $616 million, although this quarter included a $27 million one-time gain.

Stripping that gain out, net operating income per share was still five to 10 cents above forecasts at $1.27 versus $0.94 a year ago, due to a $3.19 rise in crude prices and a 49 cent rise in natural gas combined with a six percent rise in production.
The stock was off 0.125 at $66.50.
For Chevron, there was also a turnround in refining and marketing, with operating earnings of $78 million compared with $18 million a year ago.

"Despite the improvement in earnings, the company's return on capital remains very low in the capital intensive and highly competitive U.S. refining and marketing business," said chief executive Ken Derr.
Analysts say that as crude oil prices decline through the year, refining will become a larger part of earnings for integrated oil companies.
"There is also going to be a volumetric increase in refining," said Howard Weil analyst Bud Tower.
Phillips Petroleum Co saw net income of $227 million compared with $695 million a year ago although the year ago included a one-time gain of $565 million.
Stripping the gain out, operating income was $247 million or $0.94 per share against $210 million, $0.80 per share.
Growth came from a 34 percent rise in upstream to $202 million and refining rose $2.0 million to $9.0 million.

Among pure refiners, the picture was poor, Tosco Corp, the largest independent refiner in the U.S. saw net income drop to $3.6 million from $24 million, or $0.03 per share from $0.21, partly due to accidents and refinery downtime, but also because of the depressed state of the industry.
Yet it remains optimistic as a $100 million refurbishment programme at its 150,000 barrel per day Trainer refinery will be completed ahead of schedule and the company is seeing imrpoved margins.
"Crude oil prices have fallen over $6.00 per barrel, and retail margins have returned to seasonal levels normal levels," said chief executive Thomas O'Malley.
Tosco stock rallied strongly, adding $0.625 to $29.50 on the outlook for refiners and news on Trainer.
Drilling and service companies were major beneficiaries of increased exploration and production spending and results were ahead of forecasts.

Cliffs net income rose to $60.9 million from $29 million and Baker Hughes where second quarter net income was $57.9 million from $41.6 million and earnings per share rose 38 percent to $0.40 from $0.29.
Cliffs shares added $0.125 to $68.50 and Baker Hughes $0.825 to $37.50.
((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
